decision.answer_to_question: Main limitation is value sorting / adaptation of the frozen AgentRM and Qwen scalar scorers to the state-only value target, not a broad failure of evidence parsing. E accuracy is high (audit 0.9137; mechanism-macro 0.9151) and evidence citations are 99.27% valid; E_CPU beats both calibrated model baselines and improves the closed loop. However E_CPU does not beat always_query on primary regret, and both E_STATE_R and O_STATE_R are much worse than E_CPU even with oracle state. The residual evidence-parsing weakness is localized to stale-revision unknown recognition (26 dangerous audit errors, 25 unknown->positive; versioned accuracy 0.7931), not a general state-extraction failure.

decision.external_validation_gate: NOT MET: E_CPU does not beat always_query on primary regret; the overall dangerous-confusion threshold hides the versioned_report stale-evidence failure. Therefore do not call E_CPU a validated method or start external validation as a success claim.
decision.next_direction: Exit the current frozen scalar-scorer + toy combination. The one next research direction is an external real-tool task study comparing grounded state extraction plus deterministic Q (E_CPU) against always_query, with the frozen AgentRM/Qwen scorers only as negative controls; do not train or prompt-scan these scorers further and do not add more same-template toy data.
not_claims: not a universal PRM failure claim
